doc.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Interviewer's own childhood radio story
summary: Michael Woods shares sneaking radio listening; Mance recalls the radio brand.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I share this with you so you won’t feel alone. I used to do the same thing and my parents asked me what I wanted for Christmas and I said a transistor radio. And I was a little more discreet because at this time when they come out with the transistor radios, they also had earplugs. And they forbade us from listening to music after eleven o’clock. After eleven o’clock is when all the greatest rhythm & blues would come on. And so we would pretend to be asleep and we would, just before we went to sleep we would find the station that we wanted, and then we’d turn off the lights and everything, sometimes we’d even have a little flashlight under the covers to find that station. So I know what you’re talking about.

Yeah, earphones would have been great in those days, but I had to take the whole radio. It was a small one, I said I just want a small table radio, and it was about like that. I even remember the name of it, Arvin, A-R-V-I-N. That was the name of the radio. I guess they’re out of business now you know, but it was this little, small radio.
